title: Have an agent test a new tool and write a report
summary: Simon Willison had Claude Code install a small web-page runner, build test prototypes and write a report judging it as a scraper and as a safe sandbox.
agent_role: The agent cloned and ran the tool, built exploratory prototypes and wrote the evaluation report; Simon wrote the one-paragraph prompt and published the result.
outcome: Simon published the agent's research report in his public research repository.
what_they_did: Simon Willison found webframe, a small tool that runs a web page like a program and prints its output. He asked Claude Code to try it, build a few prototypes and judge it. He wanted to know if it works as a sandbox and as a page scraper like his own shot-scraper tool.
how_it_went: The agent produced a written research report, which Simon shared publicly. The post does not summarize the findings.
worth_knowing: Pointing the agent at a related tool's documentation gave it a clear yardstick to compare against.
prompt: Explore [tool repo URL]. Install it and try running it, then build a few small prototypes that test its main features. Evaluate it as a possible tool for [use case 1] and [use case 2], comparing it with [similar tool or docs link]. Write a short research report covering what worked, what failed, limitations and your recommendation. Show me your plan before installing anything system-wide.

curation.rationale: A genuine, reproducible pattern of having a coding agent test an unfamiliar tool, build prototypes and write an evaluation report, with the exact prompt shared; the post itself gives few findings.
